clue.text: Chest with walnut or softwood inlay

indicators.note: an inlay is set into the surface of the wood, so the answer lies set within the words walnut or softwood

explanation.surface: A cabinet-maker describes a chest decorated with walnut or softwood inlay.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body, between neck and hips, contains the chest, so the anatomical term fits.

clue.text: TB remains problematic for member of ethnic group

indicators.note: problematic suggests the letters are troubled and disordered

explanation.surface: Tuberculosis remains a health problem for people of one ethnic community.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a tribe, the traditional term for an ethnic or kinship group.

clue.text: Cycle race leader at home on banks of Seine

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of race

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: banks are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of Seine

explanation.surface: A cycle race leader is at home along the banks of the Seine, as in the Tour de France finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' is a washing-machine programme, not a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A washing machine programme rinses, so a rinse is one of its cycles.

clue.text: Done everything by and large

parts.note: over means done or finished
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone sums up that, on the whole, everything has been done.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean taken as a whole, generally speaking.

clue.text: Beckham messed up rejecting Hearts for good — and United — then succeeded, making a fortune

indicators.note: something messed up is put in disorder, so the letters assembled here are scrambled
rejecting throws out one letter of the footballer's name, to be replaced by another
one letter is swapped for another, so the replacement comes in its place

parts.note: H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts
U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A sports report on David Beckham having a bad game before his team wins and he earns a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting Hearts for good' swaps H for G; 'messed up' then rearranges everything bar the final S. Hearts is a Scottish football club, a red herring beside United.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a huge sum of money, so earning it is making a fortune.

clue.text: Dumbo is a character controlled by others

definitions.meaning: a fool or idiot, in British slang
a puppet figure, worked by puppeteers, as in Jim Henson's show

explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls a fool by this name, and Henson's puppets are characters worked by others.

clue.text: Fish is hot, extremely lemony and without conventional taste

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: extremely takes the extremes, the outer letters, of lemony

explanation.surface: A diner finds the fish hot, very lemony and lacking in good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Garishly means in a gaudy, showy way, lacking good taste.

clue.text: Pat's husband snared in extra cunning

indicators.note: the husband is snared in the extra, held inside it

parts.note: a bye is an extra run in cricket
art means cunning or craft

explanation.surface: Pat's husband is caught up in some extra scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' looks like a name, but 'off pat' means memorised; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Known off pat means learnt thoroughly, word for word, from memory.

clue.text: Dissatisfaction with free ticket that gets left is not common

parts.note: a comp is a complimentary, free ticket
ain't is a nonstandard, common form of is not

explanation.surface: A grumble about a free ticket that gets left is rare.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an expression of dissatisfaction.

clue.text: Camber could be small and on one side of slope

indicators.note: one side of the word slope is its edge letter, here the first

explanation.surface: A road's camber may be small and on one side of a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: Camber Sands is a beach in East Sussex; the capital C is hidden at the clue's start.
explanation.definitionFit: Camber Sands is a seaside beach, so Camber is an example of a place with this name.

clue.text: Blumenthal for one and Fort tucked into meal without starter

indicators.note: one word is tucked into another, placed inside it
the starter is the first letter, which is dropped from the word for the meal

parts.note: dinner is a meal
a keep is the fortified tower of a castle

explanation.surface: Celebrity chef Heston Blumenthal's dining room serves a hearty dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fort' is a noun here, a castle's stronghold. Heston Blumenthal, the British chef, owns a pub, The Hind's Head in Bray.
explanation.definitionFit: Blumenthal runs a pub, so he is an example of a landlord of a hostelry.

clue.text: Wordlessly sing a hymn — ultimately isn't that like all of us?

parts.note: to hum is to sing with closed lips, without words

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word hymn

explanation.surface: Humming along to a hymn without knowing the words is something everyone does.
explanation.definitionFit: Every one of us belongs to mankind, so we all share that nature.

clue.text: English tax haven claims to get boost

indicators.note: the haven claims the tax, taking it inside itself

parts.note: a lee is a sheltered side, a haven from the wind
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: An English tax haven claims a boost to its finances.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise or lift something up is to give it a boost.

clue.text: Well-known landscapes — no kidding — these could be set in the Lambourn Valley

definitions.text: these could be set in the Lambourn Valley

indicators.note: no means the word for kidding is left out of the paintings

parts.note: John Constable painted famous English landscapes, so his pictures are Constables
to con is to kid or deceive

explanation.surface: An art lover insists, quite seriously, that famous landscapes could be set in the Lambourn Valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lambourn Valley in Berkshire is a centre for training racehorses, full of yards where they are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Racehorse yards with their buildings fill the Lambourn Valley, a famous training centre.

clue.text: Britain and Italy break spy cell in America

indicators.note: Britain and Italy break the spy apart, sitting inside him

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: British and Italian agents break up a spy cell operating in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a portable phone a cell, which the British call by this name.

clue.text: Author's heartfelt plea reported word for word

indicators.note: reported signals that the author's plea is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a writer begs readers to purchase the volume

explanation.surface: A writer begs readers to purchase, and a reporter quotes the plea exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing it strictly according to the rules means following the text exactly, word for word.

clue.text: What designers of new rail link do in summary?

definitions.text: What designers of new rail link do
definitions.meaning: designers of a railway mark out its route, plotting a line
an outline of a story's events

explanation.surface: Engineers planning a new rail link sum up what they do.
explanation.definitionFit: A plotline is the outline of a story, its events given in summary.

clue.text: Joining programme in French, learner meets chaps getting into moonshine

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: the learner and chaps get into the nonsense, inside it

parts.note: moonshine means nonsense, as does rot
L is for learner, as on L-plates
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A French class welcomes a learner meeting men who are making illicit liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moonshine' is the nonsense sense, not hooch.
explanation.definitionFit: An enrolment scheme is a programme for signing people up, so a joining programme.

clue.text: Undercover detective leaving discreetly out the window

indicators.note: letters thrown out the window are scattered and disordered
the detective leaves the word discreetly, taken out of it

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector

explanation.surface: An undercover detective slips away quietly through the window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops DI from DISCREETLY, and 'out the window' rearranges SCREETLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Undercover as an adverb means covertly, in a hidden way.

clue.text: Endless squabble that is stopping go-ahead for broadcast

indicators.note: the pieces stop up the word for go-ahead, sitting inside it

parts.note: a nod is approval, the go-ahead

indicators.note: endless drops the final letter

parts.note: a tiff is a squabble
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: A never-ending row holds up permission for a programme to go on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' reads as a noun in the surface but is a past participle meaning made known.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast as a past participle means made known widely, which is announced or informed.

clue.text: Alarm about Eastern transport of goods

indicators.note: the alarm goes about the other letter, around it

parts.note: fright means alarm

explanation.surface: An alarm is raised about the Eastern carriage of cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is cargo, and also the conveying of goods by lorry, ship or train.

clue.text: Drank reportedly clear amber tipple

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the slang word for drank is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to neck a drink is slang for gulping it down

indicators.note: clear empties out the inside of the word amber, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A drinker sounds off about a clear amber beer they knocked back.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink of the gods in myth, used loosely of any delicious drink, so a tipple.

clue.text: Europe, America and World middle- and long-distance leaders ahead of Farah coming up for title

indicators.note: ahead of means the earlier pieces come before the next
middle picks the central letter of World
leaders are the first letters of the two words for the race length
in a down clue, coming up reads the name from bottom to top

parts.note: Mo Farah is the British long-distance runner

explanation.surface: The heads of athletics in Europe, America and the world crown Mo Farah, the middle- and long-distance champion.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the rank or title of an earl.

clue.text: Reduce personnel during depression

indicators.note: the personnel come during the depression, inside it

parts.note: a sink is a hollow or depression in the ground
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: A firm cuts its staff during an economic slump.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink something is to make it smaller, to reduce it.

clue.text: Game New Order covering 'Echoes'

indicators.note: the rearranged word covers the other piece, holding it inside
new suggests the letters of order are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: Echo is E in the radio alphabet, so two of them give E and E

explanation.surface: The band New Order cover a song called Echoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the band's second word as ROEDR, with the two echoes going in before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: These small deer are hunted, and game means wild animals hunted for food or sport.

clue.text: Organised variable display first

indicators.note: first puts the display word ahead of the variable

parts.note: a dial reads a figure when it displays it
y is a typical algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A tidy-minded programmer insists on displaying the variable first.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prepared and set to go is what organised means here.

clue.text: Hancock's first pint or so according to the lad himself could be dangerous

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of Hancock

parts.words: pint or so according to the lad himself
parts.note: in Tony Hancock's sketch The Blood Donor he protests that a pint of blood is very nearly an armful; Hancock was known as the lad himself

explanation.surface: Tony Hancock's opinion that giving a pint of blood could be dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Hancock was a British comedian of the 1950s and 60s, nicknamed 'the lad himself'; in the sketch The Blood Donor he balks at giving 'very nearly an armful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of causing injury or damage is dangerous, a close synonym.

clue.text: Feel Prime Minister's heading for change

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter of the name, is put up for change to a new letter

parts.note: Tony Blair was a British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister feels the need to head for change.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leaves the replacement letter for the definition and crossings to fix.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a feel for something is to have a natural aptitude or knack for it.

clue.text: In the company of a master playing golf

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for master, as in an MA
on means playing, as an actor on stage
G is golf in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer enjoys the company of a master of the game on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: A preposition meaning surrounded by or mixed with others, so in their company.

clue.text: Art collector accepting 'Thora and Romeo' may be rubbish

indicators.note: the collection accepts the pieces, taking them inside

parts.note: the Tate galleries in London hold a national art collection
Thora Hird was a much-loved English actress
R is Romeo in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A gallery acquiring a portrait of Thora and Romeo might be making a poor purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: Thora Hird was a British comic actress, best known late in life for the TV series Last of the Summer Wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-rate means of poor quality, which is what calling something rubbish says.

clue.text: Doctor yet to separate oxen producing gas

indicators.note: the rearranged word comes between the two animals, separating them

parts.note: a yak is a Himalayan ox, and two of them make the plural

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of yet are altered

explanation.surface: A vet is still to separate oxen that are producing gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges the three letters as ETY, which splits the pair of oxen.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is idle chatter, and the slang phrase means non-stop talk.

clue.text: High quality run in exceptional time

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
exceptional suggests time put out of its usual order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An athlete clocks a run in an exceptional time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptional' rearranges TIME as MEIT, and R goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellence or worth, the quality of being good, is high quality.
